what_happened: Job 20261114-041123-hvyh (code job: "Queue each reading's out_of_scope follow-ups as their own requests") failed in planning, before any code was written. The planner did not complete: its fixed 600-second deadline was reached. The event lists no critic findings, no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered, and no partial plan or progress signal was kept.
cause: The planner stage has a fixed 600s wall-clock deadline. It keeps no partial plan, gives no early signal and has no resume or retry path. Nothing sizes the request against that deadline before planning starts, or records what the planner was doing when time ran out. This request touches several surfaces: reading output, request queueing and probably the queue format. A deadline stop therefore throws away all planning spend and gives no diagnosis.
other_causes: The request may be larger than one planning run can finish. It spans reading output parsing, queue writing and the dedup or dependency rules.
open_hypotheses: The planner may have been slow because of the request's size, not because it hung. The event gives no trace of planner progress.
The planner may have been stuck on a loop or heavy repo exploration. The stored fields cannot confirm or rule this out.
A transient slowdown in the model service may have contributed. This cannot be told from the fields.
contradictions: No critic findings or planning rounds are listed, so nothing shows the plan or design was flawed. The cause is purely a time stop, unlike the earlier planning failures, which all ended on critic findings after round 5.
prevention: Make the planner stage survive its deadline. It should write its draft plan to the job record as it goes. On a deadline stop it should keep the draft and hand it to a resume or retry round, with the reason recorded as a timeout, not a plain failure. Also check the request's size against the deadline before dispatch, and split an oversized request. Gate counts show no gate disagreements (verifier 0 of 161, test 0 of 44), so this is a missing protection, not a wrong gate.
proposed_request: Make planning survive its time deadline. (1) Have the planner save its draft plan to the job record after each step. (2) When the planner reaches its deadline, mark the job as a planning timeout, not a plain failure, keep the draft, and let one retry resume from the draft with a fresh deadline. (3) Record in the job the last step the planner reached. Acceptance: a test with a fake planner that never finishes shows the job ends as a planning timeout with its draft kept and the last step recorded, and a retry starts from the draft. Then re-queue "Queue each reading's out_of_scope follow-ups as their own requests" as a separate request.
